name: rapid_fire
doc: Claims arriving FASTER than verify can clear — the one-window-dedupe failure the S2 --real run surfaced. Five distinct science_health claims land ~1.2s apart while a verify takes ~2.6s. The rolling window is cumulative, so every terminal window still LEADS with the first claim; the extractor keys off that leading claim and re-returns it, F2 claim-level dedupe (60s window) drops the repeats, and the four genuinely-new claims that share those windows never get their own extract → they are LOST. Only the first claim airs. This is SUPPOSED to fail: it pins the rapid-fire recall collapse so a per-claim windowing / verify-queue fix can be measured against it (expected: recall rises from ~20% toward 100%, aired from 1 toward 5).

expected_scorecard.status_note: known-degraded: rapid-fire one-window-dedupe collision. The honest failure signal is the GATE DISTRIBUTION — 4 of 5 distinct claims collapse to 'dedupe' (the extractor re-returns the leading claim of the cumulative window) and only 1 airs. NOTE: word_coverage and claim_recall both read HIGH here — the cumulative window physically contains every utterance's words, and each deduped check still carries *a* claim, so the coverage/recall metrics do NOT see this failure. That is exactly why the bound is on dedupe-count + aired, not recall. When per-claim windowing / a verify queue ships, dedupe should fall toward 0 and aired rise toward 5 — re-baseline then.
